narrative.overview:
Resonory is drawn as a dark, quiet archive: a wall of the visitor's own saved cards, dimmed almost to nothing on a near-black ground, with the product's interface floating over it as a few frosted palettes. Nothing on the screen is loud except the one thing the product exists to do. When a save comes back, it lights up orange, a thread draws to it, and a small dot rises above it, exactly like the dot rising above the stacked bars of the logo. That moment is the whole visual identity; everything else is held in greys so it can land.

The system is monochrome by construction. Off-white (#FAFAF7) is the only bright neutral and is set at fixed strengths (66%, 56%, 16%, 9%) for secondary text, meta and edges, rather than introducing more greys. Surfaces separate by small tonal steps (ground, card, card-raised) and hairline borders, and depth comes from long, soft, dark drops under the floating palettes. Type is Geist throughout, with Geist Mono for everything the product "knows" about a save: when, where from, how much was read, the keycap.

Density is high but calm. The screen is a single viewport, the wall supplies texture and proof at once, and motion is slow and springy: parts rise in on load, the wall drifts a few pixels over 44 seconds, and the only fast thing is the spark that runs along the orange thread.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black ground with a dimmed wall of saved cards as the backdrop, never an empty field or a gradient.
One accent, orange, reserved for resurfacing: the logo dot, the two verbs of the headline, the lit card, its thread and its rising dot.
Primary actions are off-white fills with dark text; orange never fills a button.
Floating palettes: pill nav, search-style field, browser window, Cue, all on tonal surfaces with hairline edges and soft drops.
Geist for language, Geist Mono for metadata and keycaps.
One easing curve (cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)) for every state change; every animation has a still state under reduced motion.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Orange means an Item came back, and nothing else. It is never a button fill, a link colour, a focus ring, a label or a decoration. If a new surface wants orange somewhere that is not the logo dot, a highlighted verb about saving and bringing back, or a resurfaced item, use Paper White instead.

rules.name: The One White Rule
rules.body: Secondary text and edges are the same off-white at fixed strengths (66, 56, 16, 9 percent), not new greys. A new tier of emphasis takes a new opacity of Paper White, not a new hex.

rules.name: The Error Is Not Red Rule
rules.body: Errors stay in the monochrome: the field's edge goes to Paper White at 72% and the message is Paper White text with a warning icon. Neither red nor orange signals an error.

rules.name: The Machine Speaks Mono Rule
rules.body: Anything the product records about an Item (when, where from, how far read, how many) is Geist Mono at meta size in Faint. Human-facing sentences are set in Geist, with one exception the founder's design makes: the proof line under the form (the invitation, "Join the waitlist. Be among the first to use Resonory.", or the waiting count) is the form's status line and is set in Geist Mono at Note size in Mute, with tabular figures.

rules.name: The Colour, Not Slant Rule
rules.body: Emphasis inside the headline is an `em` coloured orange with the italic removed. Use it only for the verbs of saving and bringing back.

rules.name: The Only Light Is Orange Rule
rules.body: Shadows are dark and soft; no blurred white or coloured glows, except the orange glow on a resurfaced card and its thread. The field's focus halo is a crisp 4px off-white spread, not a glow.

dos: **Do** keep the accent (#D4621A) to resurfacing: the logo dot, the verbs "saved" and "brings", a lit card, its thread and its rising dot.
**Do** make primary actions Paper White (#FAFAF7) fills with Archive Black (#141414) text, hover at 88% opacity, press at 0.97 scale.
**Do** derive secondary text and edges from Paper White at 66%, 56%, 16% and 9% before reaching for a new grey.
**Do** set every timestamp, source, count and keycap in Geist Mono at meta size.
**Do** nest rounded elements concentrically: a 14px panel with a 6px inset holds a 10px button.
**Do** use cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1) for every transition and entrance; only the wall's drift (ease-in-out) and the thread's spark (linear) differ.
**Do** give every animation a still final state under prefers-reduced-motion.
**Do** focus with a 2px Paper White outline offset 3px.
donts: **Don't** fill a button, colour a link, draw a focus ring or set a label in orange.
**Don't** signal errors in red or orange; errors stay in Paper White.
**Don't** set human-facing sentences in mono (the proof line under the form is the one exception), or slant the headline's highlighted verbs.
**Don't** add blurred white or coloured glows; the only light is the orange glow of a resurfaced card and its thread.
**Don't** use photographs in Item cards; thumbnails are the seeded sun-over-ridge placeholder.
**Don't** place a small label or kicker above a headline (uppercase, tracked or boxed). The one line above it is a plain sentence in the body lead's voice, not a label.
